questions.q: A vibrating object has frequency 50 Hz. A second object makes 10 oscillations in 20 s. Which comparison is correct?
options: A) Their frequencies are 50 Hz and 0.5 Hz respectively, so the first vibrates 100 times faster.
B) Their frequencies are 50 Hz and 2 Hz respectively, so the first vibrates 25 times faster.
C) Their frequencies are 0.02 Hz and 0.5 Hz respectively, so the second is faster.
D) Both have frequency 50 Hz because both are vibrating objects.
questions.answer: A) Their frequencies are 50 Hz and 0.5 Hz respectively, so the first vibrates 100 times faster.
questions.explanation: The first frequency is given directly as 50 vibrations per second. The second makes 10 oscillations in 20 seconds, so its frequency is 10/20 = 0.5 Hz. Comparing 50 with 0.5 gives a factor of 100.

questions.q: A frying pan is struck inside a chamber from which all air has been removed. Which statement correctly separates production from propagation of sound?
options: A) The pan will not vibrate, but sound will travel through vacuum.
B) The pan can vibrate, but the sound cannot reach an observer through the vacuum because sound needs a medium.
C) The pan cannot vibrate because vibration itself requires air.
D) The sound becomes ultrasound automatically in vacuum.
questions.answer: B) The pan can vibrate, but the sound cannot reach an observer through the vacuum because sound needs a medium.
questions.explanation: The Exemplar explicitly asks about striking a pan in vacuum and distinguishes vibration from hearing. The pan can still vibrate because the strike provides mechanical energy. However sound cannot propagate through a vacuum, so the vibration will not be heard through the evacuated space.

questions.q: A stringed instrument is plucked once with a larger force and once with a smaller force, without otherwise changing the string. Which property changes most directly?
options: A) Loudness changes because the amplitude of vibration changes.
B) Pitch changes because amplitude alone determines frequency.
C) Speed of sound changes because the string is brighter.
D) Audible range changes from 20 Hz to above 20,000 Hz automatically.
questions.answer: A) Loudness changes because the amplitude of vibration changes.
questions.explanation: The source states that loudness depends on amplitude and asks about plucking the same string with different force. A stronger pluck produces a larger vibration amplitude. Therefore the louder sound corresponds to the greater applied force, while pitch is primarily linked to frequency.

questions.q: Lightning is seen and thunder is heard 5 seconds later. Using the source value 330 m/s for the speed of sound, how far away is the event?
questions.explanation: The delay is due to sound travelling much more slowly than light, so the light is effectively seen first. Distance travelled by sound is speed multiplied by time, giving 330 m/s * 5 s = 1,650 m. Thus the event is about 1.65 km away.
